lessons.title: Qu'est-ce qu'une famille?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand that families come in many different forms and all families are special and important

opening.activity: Family circle where students share one special thing about their family without naming specific members. Introduce the word 'famille' with warm, inclusive gestures.
opening.visualSupports: Open arms for inclusion, heart gestures for love, smiling faces for celebration

main.activity: Family diversity exploration using picture books and photos showing different family structures. Students create a 'Families are Special' gallery wall, adding drawings or words about what makes families special. Emphasize that ALL families are wonderful.
main.visualSupports: Pointing to different family types with equal celebration, diversity hand gestures, appreciation expressions

decisionPoints.question: How comfortable are students sharing about their family structure?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage specific sharing while maintaining privacy boundaries
decisionPoints.ifNo: Keep discussions general and use book examples rather than personal sharing

decisionPoints.question: What level of emotional support do students need when discussing family?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use extra reassurance and validate all feelings about family
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on celebration and positive aspects of family diversity

closing.activity: Family appreciation circle where students share one word that describes how families make them feel. End with group chant: 'Toutes les familles sont spéciales!'

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students feeling that their family is different or unusual
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize that different is wonderful and provide extra examples of their family type being celebrated

lessons.realWorldConnection: Every person belongs to a family that loves and cares for them in their own special way

lessons.title: Ma famille à moi
lessons.oneGoal: Students will share and celebrate their own family structure and members with pride and confidence

opening.activity: Family pride circle where students hold a mirror and say 'Je suis fier de ma famille' (I am proud of my family). Practice proud posture and confident expressions.
opening.visualSupports: Proud chest out posture, happy confident faces, thumbs up gestures

main.activity: My family creation station where students choose how to represent their family - drawing, photos, puppet show, or storytelling. Create family portraits with emphasis on what makes each family special and loved.
main.visualSupports: Creative expression gestures, family love symbols, celebration movements

decisionPoints.question: How do we ensure all family structures feel valued and included?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Celebrate each family presentation equally with specific positive feedback
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on universal family themes like love, care, and togetherness

decisionPoints.question: Should students draw, tell, or show photos of their families?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Offer multiple options and let students choose their comfort level
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use drawing as the main activity with optional sharing

closing.activity: Family gallery walk where students admire each other's family representations and share one positive observation about a classmate's family.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students reluctant to share family information
troubleshooting.then: Respect privacy completely and offer alternative ways to participate like helping others or general family discussions

lessons.realWorldConnection: Being proud of our family helps us feel confident and secure in who we are

lessons.title: Les personnes dans ma famille
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify different family members and understand the special relationships within families

opening.activity: Family member movement game where students act out different family roles (parent, grandparent, sibling, etc.) while others guess. Use inclusive language and actions.
opening.visualSupports: Age-appropriate movements, caring gestures, family relationship symbols

main.activity: Family relationship mapping where students create a simple family tree or family circle showing the people in their family. Focus on relationships and connections rather than traditional structures.
main.visualSupports: Connection gestures, relationship pointing, family bond symbols

decisionPoints.question: Which family roles are most common in our classroom community?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include those roles prominently while also showing other family structures
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use diverse examples from books and media to show variety

decisionPoints.question: How do we include non-traditional family structures in our vocabulary?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Introduce inclusive terms like 'family member' alongside specific roles
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on universal relationship concepts like love, care, and support

closing.activity: Family bond celebration where students share one special thing about a family member's relationship to them.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students whose family structures don't match traditional vocabulary
troubleshooting.then: Expand vocabulary to include 'special adult,' 'family member,' and other inclusive terms

lessons.realWorldConnection: Each family member has a special place and important role in the family

lessons.title: Qui fait quoi dans ma famille?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore different family roles and understand how everyone contributes to family life

opening.activity: Family work charades where students act out different things family members do together - cooking, cleaning, playing, working, caring for each other.
opening.visualSupports: Work action gestures, helping hands motions, teamwork symbols

main.activity: Family contribution wheel where students create a visual showing how everyone in their family helps make family life work. Include emotional contributions, fun contributions, and practical help.
main.visualSupports: Circular motion for wheel, helping gestures, appreciation movements

decisionPoints.question: How do we present family work without reinforcing gender stereotypes?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Show diverse examples of who does what work and emphasize flexibility
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on the concept that everyone helps without specific task assignments

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on traditional chores or emotional support roles?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include both practical help and emotional support like hugs, listening, playing
decisionPoints.ifNo: Emphasize emotional support and care as equally important family work

closing.activity: Family teamwork celebration where students share how their family works together as a team.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students feeling that they don't help enough or their family doesn't work together
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize that even small helps are important and that families are always learning to work together better

lessons.realWorldConnection: Families work best when everyone helps and contributes in their own special way

lessons.title: Comment ma famille prend soin de moi
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize the many ways their family members care for and support them

opening.activity: Care and comfort sharing circle where students think about times they felt cared for by family. Use gentle, warm expressions and universal examples.
opening.visualSupports: Gentle hugging motions, care-giving gestures, comfort expressions

main.activity: Family care mapping where students create a visual showing different ways their family takes care of them - physical care, emotional care, safety, fun, learning support.
main.visualSupports: Care-giving motions, protection gestures, love symbols

decisionPoints.question: How do we highlight care without making students feel guilty about family challenges?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on what students notice and appreciate without judgment about what's missing
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use universal examples of care that all students can relate to

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on physical care or emotional care first?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include both and let students share what feels most important to them
decisionPoints.ifNo: Start with emotional care as it's more universal across family situations

closing.activity: Gratitude expression where students share one way they feel cared for and practice saying 'merci' to family in their hearts.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students from families experiencing stress or challenges
troubleshooting.then: Focus on any positive care they receive and validate that families try their best even when things are hard

lessons.realWorldConnection: Being cared for by family helps us grow strong, healthy, and confident

lessons.title: Comment j'aide ma famille
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify ways they contribute to their family and understand their important role as family members

opening.activity: Helper hero circle where students share one way they help their family and strike a superhero pose to show their importance as family helpers.
opening.visualSupports: Strong helper postures, superhero gestures, pride expressions

main.activity: Family contribution portfolio where students document the many ways they help their family - practical help, emotional support, bringing joy, learning and growing.
main.visualSupports: Helping hand gestures, contribution movements, impact symbols

decisionPoints.question: What level of responsibility do Grade 1 students actually have at home?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include both big and small ways they help, emphasizing that all help matters
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on emotional contributions and simple helps that all students can relate to

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on helping tasks or emotional contributions?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include both practical help and emotional support like hugs, smiles, cooperation
decisionPoints.ifNo: Emphasize emotional contributions as equally valuable as practical help

closing.activity: Helper appreciation ceremony where students celebrate their role as important family contributors.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students feeling they don't help enough or aren't important to their family
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize that just being themselves and growing is a huge help to families, and love doesn't depend on tasks

lessons.realWorldConnection: Even young people have important ways to help and support their families

lessons.title: Les familles de mes amis
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore and appreciate the diversity of family structures in their classroom community

opening.activity: Friendship and family appreciation circle where students think about their friends' families with curiosity and appreciation.
opening.visualSupports: Open curiosity gestures, appreciation movements, friendship symbols

main.activity: Family diversity celebration through anonymous family sharing - students contribute family facts to a class diversity chart without names, showing the beautiful variety in our classroom community.
main.visualSupports: Diversity gestures, celebration movements, inclusion symbols

decisionPoints.question: How do we celebrate differences without making any student feel 'different'?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Emphasize that diversity makes our classroom community richer and more interesting
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on common family themes while gently acknowledging variety

decisionPoints.question: Should students share about friends' families or discuss in general terms?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Keep all sharing general and anonymous to protect privacy
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use book examples and imaginary families to explore diversity

closing.activity: Community appreciation where students celebrate how family diversity makes their classroom community special and interesting.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students making comparisons or judgments about different family types
troubleshooting.then: Redirect to appreciation and emphasize that different families have different strengths and all are wonderful

lessons.realWorldConnection: Learning about different families helps us understand and appreciate our community better

lessons.title: Les traditions de ma famille
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify and share family traditions and understand how traditions connect families across time

opening.activity: Tradition discovery circle where students think about special things their family does together regularly - big or small, formal or informal.
opening.visualSupports: Repetitive motion gestures, memory symbols, tradition representations

main.activity: Family tradition gallery where students create representations of their family traditions - daily routines, special celebrations, ways of doing things, or family sayings.
main.visualSupports: Tradition gestures, celebration movements, memory symbols

decisionPoints.question: How do we include families with few established traditions or recent immigration?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Emphasize that new traditions can start anytime and small daily practices count
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on universal family practices like bedtime routines, meals, or weekend activities

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on holiday traditions or daily family habits?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include both special occasions and daily family practices as traditions
decisionPoints.ifNo: Emphasize daily traditions since they're more universal and accessible

closing.activity: Tradition appreciation walk where students view each other's traditions and share appreciation for the variety of ways families create special moments.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students feeling their family doesn't have traditions
troubleshooting.then: Help them identify simple family practices like bedtime routines, favorite foods, or ways of greeting each other as traditions

lessons.realWorldConnection: Family traditions help us remember who we are and stay connected to our family history

lessons.title: Comment ma famille célèbre
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore different ways families celebrate special moments and understand celebration as family bonding

opening.activity: Celebration dance circle where students move and express joy while thinking about how their families celebrate and have fun together.
opening.visualSupports: Joyful dancing, celebration gestures, happiness expressions

main.activity: Family celebration showcase where students create displays showing how their families mark special times - birthdays, achievements, holidays, or everyday joys.
main.visualSupports: Celebration movements, joy expressions, family happiness symbols

decisionPoints.question: How do we include families who celebrate in quiet or non-religious ways?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Show that celebrations can be big or small, loud or quiet, and all are wonderful
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on universal celebration concepts like appreciation, joy, and togetherness

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on big celebrations or small daily moments?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include both major celebrations and small daily joys like family dinners or bedtime stories
decisionPoints.ifNo: Emphasize small daily celebrations since they're more accessible to all families

closing.activity: Joy sharing circle where students share how celebrations make them feel and practice gratitude for family joy.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students whose families don't celebrate much or celebrate differently
troubleshooting.then: Help them identify any moments of family joy or togetherness as celebrations, no matter how small

lessons.realWorldConnection: Celebrating together helps families feel close and creates happy memories to treasure

lessons.title: La nourriture dans ma famille
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore family food traditions and understand how sharing meals connects families

opening.activity: Food appreciation circle where students think about favorite family foods and practice gratitude for food and family meals together.
opening.visualSupports: Eating gestures, appreciation movements, sharing symbols

main.activity: Family food traditions exploration where students create representations of special family foods, family meal practices, or ways their family shares food together.
main.visualSupports: Food sharing gestures, cultural appreciation movements, family meal symbols

decisionPoints.question: How do we handle students with food insecurity or dietary restrictions sensitively?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on any positive food experiences and family meal memories, however simple
decisionPoints.ifNo: Emphasize the connection and love in family meals rather than specific foods

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on special occasion foods or daily family meals?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include both special foods and everyday family meal practices
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on everyday family meal connection since it's more universal

closing.activity: Family meal appreciation where students share how food brings their family together and practice gratitude for family meals.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students whose families have limited food resources or no regular family meals
troubleshooting.then: Focus on any positive food memories or the idea that sharing any food shows love and care

lessons.realWorldConnection: Sharing food is one of the ways families show love and stay connected every day

lessons.title: Où vit ma famille?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore different types of homes and understand that all homes provide families with shelter and belonging

opening.activity: Home appreciation circle where students think about what makes their family's place feel like home - love, safety, belonging, not the building itself.
opening.visualSupports: Home safety gestures, belonging movements, love symbols

main.activity: Family home celebration where students create representations of what makes their family's living space special - the people, feelings, safety, and love, not the building type.
main.visualSupports: Home comfort gestures, family space symbols, belonging movements

decisionPoints.question: How do we discuss housing without highlighting economic differences?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus entirely on feelings of home rather than physical building characteristics
decisionPoints.ifNo: Emphasize that homes are about family love and safety, not size or type of building

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on house types or what makes a place feel like home?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus completely on feelings, safety, love, and family connection in any space
decisionPoints.ifNo: Avoid discussing building types and focus on universal home feelings

closing.activity: Home gratitude circle where students share what makes them feel at home with their family, regardless of where they live.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students whose housing situation is unstable or temporary
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize that home is wherever their family is together with love and safety

lessons.realWorldConnection: Having a safe place to live with family helps us feel secure and ready to learn and grow

lessons.title: Les espaces spéciaux de ma famille
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify special family spaces and understand how physical spaces can hold family memories and meaning

opening.activity: Special space memory circle where students think about places where their family spends time together and feels happy and connected.
opening.visualSupports: Memory gestures, space appreciation movements, family connection symbols

main.activity: Family space appreciation where students create representations of special family spaces - not fancy rooms, but places where family feels close and makes memories.
main.visualSupports: Family togetherness gestures, memory symbols, special space movements

decisionPoints.question: How do we help students find meaning in any family space, regardless of size or luxury?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on family connection and memories in any space, however small or simple
decisionPoints.ifNo: Emphasize that special spaces are about family time together, not about fancy rooms

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on rooms, outdoor spaces, or specific objects?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include any space where family feels close - indoor, outdoor, or even a special chair
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on the concept of family togetherness in any meaningful space

closing.activity: Special space appreciation where students share how family spaces help them feel connected and loved.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students who don't have permanent or private family spaces
troubleshooting.then: Help them identify any place where family feels close together, even if shared or temporary

lessons.realWorldConnection: Special family spaces help us feel connected to our family and hold our important memories

lessons.title: Comment les familles communiquent
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore different ways families communicate and understand communication as essential for family connection

opening.activity: Communication practice circle where students explore different ways families talk, listen, and share feelings with each other.
opening.visualSupports: Speaking gestures, listening movements, expression symbols

main.activity: Family communication celebration where students explore the many ways their families share thoughts and feelings - talking, listening, hugs, notes, or special looks.
main.visualSupports: Communication gestures, family connection movements, sharing symbols

decisionPoints.question: How do we include families who communicate in multiple languages?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Celebrate multilingual communication as a special family gift and strength
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on universal communication concepts like listening, caring, and understanding

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on verbal communication or include non-verbal family communication?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include talking, listening, hugs, smiles, and other ways families share feelings
decisionPoints.ifNo: Emphasize all forms of family communication as important and valuable

closing.activity: Communication appreciation where students share how their family communicates love and connection.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students whose families may have communication challenges
troubleshooting.then: Focus on any positive family communication and emphasize that families are always learning better ways to connect

lessons.realWorldConnection: Good communication helps families solve problems, share love, and stay close to each other

lessons.title: Les familles dans notre communauté
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand how families connect with other families and contribute to community life

opening.activity: Community connection circle where students think about how their family connects with neighbors, friends, and community members.
opening.visualSupports: Connection gestures, community movements, network symbols

main.activity: Family community web where students explore how their families connect with other families and contribute to making their community better and stronger.
main.visualSupports: Web connection gestures, community building movements, contribution symbols

decisionPoints.question: How connected are students' families to the local community?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Build on existing connections and celebrate family community involvement
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on simple community connections like school, neighbors, or local places

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on neighborhood connections or broader community involvement?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include both close neighbors and broader community connections like school and local businesses
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on immediate community connections that students can observe and understand

closing.activity: Community appreciation where students celebrate how families working together make communities strong and caring.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students whose families may be isolated or new to the community
troubleshooting.then: Focus on school community connections and emphasize that community connections can grow over time

lessons.realWorldConnection: Families are stronger when they connect with other families and help their community

lessons.title: Créer un livre de famille
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create a family book celebrating their family's unique story and characteristics

opening.activity: Story celebration circle where students think about their family as having a special, important story worth sharing and remembering.
opening.visualSupports: Story-telling gestures, celebration movements, book creation symbols

main.activity: Family story book creation where students compile their family learning into a personal book celebrating their family's uniqueness, love, and special characteristics.
main.visualSupports: Book creation gestures, family celebration movements, story organization symbols

decisionPoints.question: What format would work best for students with different fine motor skills?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Offer multiple formats including drawing, dictating, photo books, or digital creation
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on simple formats that emphasize content over complex construction

decisionPoints.question: Should books focus on current family or include family history?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus primarily on current family with option to include family history if available
decisionPoints.ifNo: Emphasize current family relationships and experiences students know well

closing.activity: Author celebration where students appreciate their creation and their family's special story.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students who may need help gathering family information
troubleshooting.then: Support with family interviews or help them create books based on their own family experiences and observations

lessons.realWorldConnection: Creating family stories helps us remember and share what makes our family special

lessons.title: Exposition de familles
lessons.oneGoal: Students will share their family celebrations with classmates and appreciate the diversity of all families

opening.activity: Gallery preparation circle where students prepare to share their family stories with appreciation and to receive others' stories with respect and curiosity.
opening.visualSupports: Gallery gestures, appreciation movements, respectful sharing symbols

main.activity: Family story gallery where students share their family books and celebrate the beautiful diversity of families in their classroom community.
main.visualSupports: Gallery sharing gestures, family appreciation movements, diversity celebration symbols

decisionPoints.question: How do we create a safe, celebratory atmosphere for family sharing?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Establish clear appreciation guidelines and model respectful, positive responses
decisionPoints.ifNo: Keep sharing optional and provide alternative ways for students to participate

decisionPoints.question: Should presentations be formal or informal, individual or small group?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use informal sharing in small groups to reduce pressure and increase connection
decisionPoints.ifNo: Allow students to choose their comfort level for sharing

closing.activity: Family diversity celebration where students appreciate the variety and beauty of all the families in their classroom.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students feeling nervous about sharing or comparing families
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize that every family is wonderful and provide support for comfortable sharing levels

lessons.realWorldConnection: Sharing our family stories helps others understand and appreciate different ways of being a family

lessons.title: Jeu de rôles: Ma famille
lessons.oneGoal: Students will role-play family scenarios to practice family vocabulary and explore family relationships

opening.activity: Family role-play preparation where students explore different family roles with appreciation and understanding.
opening.visualSupports: Role-play gestures, family relationship movements, character appreciation symbols

main.activity: Family scenario exploration where students act out positive family interactions, practice family vocabulary, and explore family relationships through creative play.
main.visualSupports: Family interaction gestures, role-play movements, vocabulary practice symbols

decisionPoints.question: Which family scenarios would be most engaging and appropriate for role-play?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on positive family interactions like meals, celebrations, problem-solving, and care-giving
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use universal family scenarios that all students can relate to and enjoy

decisionPoints.question: Should students play their own family roles or explore different family structures?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Allow students to explore different family roles to build empathy and understanding
decisionPoints.ifNo: Let students choose whether to play familiar or unfamiliar family roles

closing.activity: Role-play reflection where students share what they learned about family relationships through creative exploration.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students uncomfortable with role-play or family scenarios
troubleshooting.then: Provide alternative participation like being directors, helping with props, or observing and commenting

lessons.realWorldConnection: Playing family roles helps us understand different perspectives and practice family relationships

lessons.title: Lettres à ma famille
lessons.oneGoal: Students will write simple letters to family members expressing appreciation and love

opening.activity: Letter writing inspiration circle where students think about what they want their family members to know about their love and appreciation.
opening.visualSupports: Letter writing gestures, appreciation movements, love expression symbols

main.activity: Family appreciation letters where students create simple letters, cards, or messages expressing their feelings for family members using words, pictures, or symbols.
main.visualSupports: Writing gestures, appreciation movements, love expression symbols

decisionPoints.question: What writing level is appropriate for Grade 1 students' letter writing?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Support with templates, pictures, and simple words while encouraging personal expression
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on the expression of feelings rather than perfect writing mechanics

decisionPoints.question: Should letters focus on gratitude, love, or sharing school learning?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include appreciation, love, and sharing of school family learning
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus primarily on expressing love and appreciation for family

closing.activity: Letter appreciation where students share (if comfortable) their messages and prepare to deliver their family love.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students who may need help expressing their feelings
troubleshooting.then: Provide feeling words, pictures, and templates to support emotional expression

lessons.realWorldConnection: Telling family members how we feel about them helps strengthen family relationships

lessons.title: Célébration des familles
lessons.oneGoal: Students will plan and participate in a classroom celebration honoring all types of families

opening.activity: Celebration planning circle where students think about how to honor and celebrate all the wonderful families in their classroom.
opening.visualSupports: Celebration gestures, planning movements, family honor symbols

main.activity: Family celebration preparation where students work together to create a classroom event that honors all family types and celebrates family diversity and love.
main.visualSupports: Celebration preparation gestures, family honor movements, diversity celebration symbols

decisionPoints.question: What type of celebration would include and honor all family structures?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on universal family themes like love, care, support, and belonging
decisionPoints.ifNo: Create celebration activities that work for all family types without exclusion

decisionPoints.question: Should families be invited to participate or should this be a classroom-only event?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Consider family availability and comfort while focusing on student celebration of families
decisionPoints.ifNo: Keep celebration student-focused while honoring families through student appreciation

closing.activity: Celebration culmination where students participate in their family appreciation celebration and share joy about family diversity.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students whose families cannot participate or feel different
troubleshooting.then: Ensure celebration focuses on student appreciation for families rather than family presence or participation

lessons.realWorldConnection: Celebrating families together helps us appreciate that all families are important and valuable

lessons.title: Je suis fier de ma famille
lessons.oneGoal: Students will reflect on their learning about families and express pride in their own family relationships

opening.activity: Pride reflection circle where students think about how their understanding of families has grown and how they feel about their own family.
opening.visualSupports: Pride gestures, reflection movements, growth symbols

main.activity: Family pride culmination where students reflect on their family learning journey and create a final expression of family pride and appreciation.
main.visualSupports: Pride expressions, reflection gestures, family appreciation movements

decisionPoints.question: How do we help students articulate what they've learned about families?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use reflection prompts and examples to help students recognize their learning growth
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on feelings and appreciation rather than academic articulation

decisionPoints.question: Should reflection focus on personal growth or family appreciation?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include both personal learning growth and deepened family appreciation
decisionPoints.ifNo: Emphasize family appreciation and pride as the primary focus

closing.activity: Family pride celebration where students share their final reflections and celebrate their growth in understanding and appreciating families.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students who still feel uncertain about their family or family pride
troubleshooting.then: Provide individual support and emphasize that all families are learning and growing, just like students

lessons.realWorldConnection: Being proud of our family gives us confidence and helps us appreciate other families too
